questions.stem: Why do transformers only work with alternating current (AC)?

options.text: AC has a higher voltage than DC
AC creates a constantly changing magnetic field in the core, which is needed to induce a voltage in the secondary coil
DC would melt the iron core
AC flows through the iron core but DC cannot

questions.explanation: Transformers rely on electromagnetic induction, which requires a changing magnetic flux. AC constantly changes direction, creating a continuously changing magnetic field in the iron core. This changing field induces a voltage in the secondary coil. DC produces a steady field and so cannot induce a continuous voltage.
